ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the device shown in the figure, the cd rod is originally at rest. If the cd rod is to move to the right, what kind of motion should the ab rod make?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, on the left side there are two horizontal guide rails and one vertical metal rod cd, with c on top and d on bottom. The region where cd is located is drawn with “×”, indicating that the uniform magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface inward. On the right side there are also two horizontal guide rails and one vertical metal rod ab, with a on top and b on bottom. The region where ab is located is drawn with “·”, indicating that the uniform magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface outward. In the middle there is the same iron core; the left coil is labeled L2 and is connected in the left circuit where cd is located, and the right coil is labeled L1 and is connected in the right circuit where ab is located. The two coils are wound on the same iron core to form mutual induction. Then reason: To make the cd rod move to the right, the cd rod must be subjected to an Ampere force to the right in the inward magnetic field on the left side. By the left-hand rule or F=IL×B, when the magnetic field is inward, if the current in the cd rod is downward from c to d, then the direction of the Ampere force is to the right. Therefore the target requires that the current in the cd rod in the left circuit be c→d. According to the connection method of the left circuit in the figure and the winding direction of L2, the current c→d in cd corresponds to an induced current of the corresponding direction appearing in L2; by using Lenz's law to infer reversely the trend of magnetic flux change corresponding to this induced current, it can be known that the magnetic flux of the original direction produced by L1 in the iron core should be weakening. Then according to the winding direction of L1 in the figure, to produce this original-direction magnetic flux, the current in the ab rod in the right circuit should be upward from b to a; and since the magnetic flux is weakening, it indicates that the current in the right circuit is decreasing. Finally determine how ab should move to make the current in the rod be from b to a: The magnetic field on the right side is represented by “·”, with the direction perpendicular to the paper surface outward. If the ab rod moves to the left, the positive charges in the rod are acted on by v×B and move upward along the rod, so the direction of the induced current in the ab rod is b→a. Also because the required current is decreasing, and the magnitude of the induced current is related to the speed of motion, the speed of the ab rod should gradually decrease. Final answer: The ab rod should make decelerating motion to the left.
